'''Bernard Sapoval''' (30 October 1937 – 26 August 2020) was a French physicist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.polytechnique.edu/fr/content/deces-de-bernard-sapoval-lun-des-piliers-de-lhistoire-de-lx|title=Décès de Bernard Sapoval, l'un des piliers de l'histoire de l'X|date=1 September 2020|work=École Polytechnique|language=French}}</ref> He was known for his work in semi-conductors, and fractals.

==Biography==
An engineer, Sapoval graduated from [[ESPCI Paris]] in 1960.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espci.org/fr/anciens/eleves/75/|title=Les ingénieurs de la 75e promotion de l'ESPCI Paris|work=ESPCI Paris|language=French}}</ref> He continued his studies at the [[École Polytechnique]] to study the fields of magnetic resonance of semiconductors.

Beginning in 1970, Sapoval was a professor at the École Polytechnique. In 1976, he became director of the condensed matter physics lab at the school. In 1978, he became president of the physics department. In 1997, he began working at the [[École normale supérieure Paris-Saclay]] and served as research director of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pmc.polytechnique.fr/pagesperso/bs/|title=Bernard Sapoval|work=CNRS|language=French}}</ref>

In the 1970s, he met [[Benoit Mandelbrot]] and began studying [[fractal]]s, which he researched on the coast of [[Brittany]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blogs.mediapart.fr/vincent-fleury/blog/090912/la-recherche-qui-ne-fait-pas-de-bruit|title=La recherche qui ne fait pas de bruit|date=9 September 2012|work=Mediapart|language=French}}</ref> In 1997, he published ''Universalité et Fractales, Jeux d'enfants ou délits d'initié'', which made fractal geometry more accessible to the general public and won him the Prix de la Culture scientifique in 1998.<ref>{{cite book |last=Sapoval|first=Bernard|date=1997|title=Universalités et fractales|trans-title= |url=https://editions.flammarion.com/Catalogue/nouvelle-bibliotheque-scientifique/universalites-et-fractales|language=French|location=Paris|publisher=Flammarion|isbn=9782082112079}}</ref> In 2003, he received the Grand Prix de l'innovation for his research on the fractal wall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://geoffreyhistoire.pagesperso-orange.fr/fractales/biographies.html|title=Benoît Mandelbrot|work=Geoffrey Bruno & Loic Devilliers|language=French}}</ref> In 1995, he was made a [[List of American Physical Society Fellows (1972–1997)|Fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=S&year=1997&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|access-date=24 September 2020}}</ref>

Bernard Sapoval died on 26 August 2020 in [[Paris]] at the age of 82.

==Publications==
*''Physique des semi-conducteurs'' (1984)
*''Les fractales'' (1990)
*''Physique des semi-conducteurs'' (1991)
*''Physics of semiconductors'' (1995)
*''Universalités et fractales, jeux d’enfant ou délits d’initié'' (1997)
*''Universalités et fractales'' (2001)
*''Elements of semiconductor physics'' (2002)
